question: Can a single seed branch discover the smallest useful shared-copper bundle automatically, without expanding through the whole rooted tree?

manual_control.evaluation: The selector changes only how the useful local bundle is chosen. Given the same bundle, it reproduces the manual engine input and result exactly.

bounded_control.evaluation: The branch-count bound is checked before lowering. An oversized neighborhood cannot partially run or silently fall back to the weaker seed-only experiment.

conclusion.advantage: A raw leaf seed now finds its closest physical-copper sibling bundle automatically and unlocks the same movable shared junction as manual selection.
conclusion.penalty: Selection currently compares branch segment pairs on the CPU. The real tree required 830 contact tests before the much larger relaxation pass; this is acceptable here but needs spatial indexing or graph-native storage before whole-net use.
conclusion.scope: The policy follows nearest same-layer physical contacts from leaf toward root in an acyclic root-to-terminal representation. It does not yet cover graph cycles, via-only contact, choosing seeds, or proving that one hop is the best optimization neighborhood.
conclusion.next: Use the selector to form small discriminating subtrees for bounded via-removal and via-relocation actions, retaining fixed-via relaxation as the control.
